**Visual Analysis of the Test Image:**
- Wheat leaf with a prominent broad, longitudinal stripe running the full length of the leaf
- The stripe is pale yellow to whitish/tan in color
- Green tissue remains intact on the left side of the leaf
- Sharp, defined boundary between the affected (pale) and healthy (green) tissue
- Linear pattern running parallel to the leaf veins — no pustules, spots, or discrete lesions visible

**Differential Reasoning:**
- **Cephalosporium Stripe**: Caused by *Cephalosporium gramineum*; classic symptom is a single broad yellow-to-white stripe running parallel to leaf veins with a sharp margin — matches very well
- **Stripe Rust**: Would show discrete yellow-orange pustule stripes, not a broad diffuse pale stripe
- **Bacterial_Leaf_Streak_Black_Chaff**: More water-soaked tan-to-brown lesions, less clean striping
- **Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus**: Causes mosaic/mottled yellowing, less regular than this single stripe
- **Barley Yellow Dwarf Virus**: Yellowing typically from leaf tip downward, more diffuse

The single, broad, pale-yellow stripe with a sharp margin running the length of the leaf parallel to the veins is most characteristic of **Cephalosporium Stripe**.
